packageRules.description: First-party actions, no need to quarantine: we own them, and one referenced by branch would otherwise sit pending until its default branch goes two weeks without a commit
Go modules are never grouped: each module gets its own PR so a bad bump can be reverted on its own
First-party deps are grouped and never quarantined: we track unreleased pseudo-versions that change constantly, so one PR per module would flood the queue
Exception to the rule above: the pion modules are co-released and depend on each other, so bumping them one at a time produces PRs that don't build
Never bump the go/toolchain directives in go.mod: this module is a library, so the go directive is the minimum we ask of consumers and must stay at the lowest version our dependencies require.

protobuf-es majors change the generated code and the published @livekit/protocol API, so they get their own PR instead of riding along with routine npm bumps. The runtime and the generator must move together.

TypeScript majors get their own PR: TypeScript 7 no longer exposes the JS compiler API that unbuild's declaration bundling depends on, so a major can block every other npm bump until the build tooling catches up.
